# Mixing Tank Control Narrative (Draft for FDS)

This is reverse-engineered from seven rungs and the technician's notes. Intent is inferred, not confirmed. Field wiring polarity is known only for LSL_TANK and the STOP button. Anything marked "verify" needs a walkdown or an operator interview before it goes into the FDS.

## Top findings

1. **Restart after power cycle (F-01):** `B3:0/0` is a bit-file address, and SLC-500 bit files are retained through power loss by default. The export shows no first-scan rung that clears it. That matches the tank filling by itself last month.
2. **Fill timeout is defeated by START (F-02):** START resets the timer and silences the horn at any time, even while running.
3. **Selector bypasses low-level protection (F-05, F-06):** `AGIT_HAND` bypasses the low-level interlock on the agitator, and the steam valve follows the agitator. The selector can therefore put steam into a nearly empty tank.
4. **No fail-safe signal loss (F-04):** Fill and steam do not demonstrably fail safe on a broken high-level or temperature wire.

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

Module MXT-100 (placeholder tag) fills a tank, agitates the contents, and heats them with steam. It uses level switches and a temperature switch. It has no analog loops. The exported logic has no discharge, recipe, or end-of-batch function (OI-01).

## 2. Equipment and tags

No instrument index exists. This table is the interim index. ISA tag numbers are assigned under OI-07.

| Legacy address | Legacy name | Function | Required state on signal loss |
|---|---|---|---|
| I:1/0 | START_PB | Momentary start | Not pressed |
| I:1/1 | STOP_PB | NC, ON when healthy | Stop |
| I:1/2 | ESTOP_OK | ON when healthy | E-stop |
| I:1/3 | LSL_TANK | ON when level is above low point | Reads "below low" |
| I:1/4 | LSH_TANK | High level (polarity: verify) | Reads "high" |
| I:1/5 | AGIT_HAND | Door selector switch | Off |
| I:1/6 | TEMP_LOW | Temperature below heat setpoint (assumed: verify) | Reads "not low" |
| O:2/0 | FILL_VLV | Fill valve | Closed |
| O:2/1 | AGITATOR | Agitator starter | Off |
| O:2/2 | STEAM_VLV | Steam valve | Closed |
| O:2/3 | ALARM_HORN | Horn | Per alarm philosophy |

Setpoint list (all numbers live here):

| ID | Item | Value |
|---|---|---|
| SP-MXT-001 | Fill timeout | 600 s as-found (confirm, OI-06) |
| SP-MXT-002 | LSL_TANK on-delay | TBD |
| SP-MXT-003 | LSL_TANK off-delay | TBD |
| SP-MXT-004 | Maximum continuous steam time | TBD (OI-05) |

## 3. States and transitions

| State | Outputs | Allowed exits |
|---|---|---|
| STOPPED | All off | RUNNING (T1) |
| RUNNING | Per FR-MXT-005 to -013 | STOPPED (T2), FILL FAULT (T3), E-STOPPED (T5) |
| FILL FAULT | FILL_VLV closed, horn on. Agitator and steam follow RUNNING rules (OI-04). | STOPPED (T4), E-STOPPED (T5) |
| E-STOPPED | All off | STOPPED (T6) |

| ID | From → To | Initiator | Condition | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T0 | Power-up → STOPPED | Auto | Always | Automatic |
| T1 | STOPPED → RUNNING | Operator | START pressed, STOP_PB healthy, ESTOP_OK healthy | Operator-initiated |
| T2 | RUNNING → STOPPED | Operator | STOP_PB pressed or circuit open | Manual |
| T3 | RUNNING → FILL FAULT | Auto | Fill timer expired | Automatic |
| T4 | FILL FAULT → STOPPED | Operator | STOP_PB pressed | Manual |
| T5 | Any → E-STOPPED | Auto | ESTOP_OK lost | Automatic |
| T6 | E-STOPPED → STOPPED | Auto | ESTOP_OK restored. Operator must then press START. | Automatic |

## 4. Regulatory control

None. Heating is on/off from TEMP_LOW. The switch deadband is unknown (OI-02).

## 5. Sequence SQ-MXT-01 (fill, level-driven)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | Open FILL_VLV. Start fill timer. | LSH_TANK not high | Included in step 20 | Go to step 30 if LSH_TANK is already high |
| 20 | Wait for high level. | LSH_TANK high | SP-MXT-001 | Close FILL_VLV. Enter FILL FAULT. Start horn. |
| 30 | Close FILL_VLV. Reset fill timer. | Level falls below high, then step 10 | None. The wait is indefinite by design, and there is no valve position feedback. | Not applicable |

The module refills whenever level drops. Confirm that this is intended (OI-01).

## 6. Requirements

Basis codes: **C** = carried forward, **X** = changed (finding ID), **N** = new.

| ID | Requirement | Basis | FAT test |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-MXT-001 | After power-up or a processor RUN transition, enter STOPPED. Keep all outputs off. | X (F-01) | Run the module. Cycle power. Verify that outputs stay off until START. |
| FR-MXT-002 | Accept START only in STOPPED with STOP_PB and ESTOP_OK healthy. Ignore START in all other states. | X (F-02) | Press START in RUNNING and FILL FAULT. Verify no change in state or timer. |
| FR-MXT-003 | Enter STOPPED and de-energize all outputs when STOP_PB is pressed or its circuit opens. | C (R0) | Press STOP. Lift the STOP wire. |
| FR-MXT-004 | Enter E-STOPPED and de-energize all outputs when ESTOP_OK is lost. | C (R0) | Trip the E-stop in each state. |
| FR-MXT-005 | Open FILL_VLV only in RUNNING, with LSH_TANK not high and the fill timer not expired. Close it otherwise. | C (R1) | Simulate levels. Verify valve state. |
| FR-MXT-006 | Run the fill timer only while FILL_VLV is open. Reset it when LSH_TANK goes high and on entry to STOPPED. Limit: SP-MXT-001. | X (F-03) | Hold level low until timeout. Then run two short fills. Verify the timer resets each time. |
| FR-MXT-007 | On fill timer expiry, close FILL_VLV, enter FILL FAULT, and start the horn. | C (R1, R2, R5) | Hold level low. Verify the sequence. |
| FR-MXT-008 | Clear FILL FAULT only through STOP, then START. | X (F-02) | Press START in FILL FAULT. Verify no clear. |
| FR-MXT-009 | Silence the horn with ACK. Keep the alarm active until reset. | N (F-08) | Press ACK. Verify horn off and alarm active. |
| FR-MXT-010 | Run AGITATOR only in RUNNING or FILL FAULT, with LSL_TANK above low for SP-MXT-002. Stop it after LSL_TANK is below low for SP-MXT-003. | X (F-05, F-10) | Vary level around the low point. Verify no chatter. |
| FR-MXT-011 | Do not let AGIT_HAND bypass FR-MXT-010 (pending OI-03). | X (F-05) | Set AGIT_HAND with level low. Verify agitator off. |
| FR-MXT-012 | Open STEAM_VLV only when AGITATOR runs, LSL_TANK is above low, and TEMP_LOW is true. Close it otherwise. | C (R4), X (F-06) | Set AGIT_HAND with level low. Verify steam closed. |
| FR-MXT-013 | Close STEAM_VLV and raise an alarm when continuous steam time exceeds SP-MXT-004. | N (F-07) | Hold TEMP_LOW true. Verify closure at the limit. |
| FR-MXT-014 | Treat loss of LSH_TANK as high, LSL_TANK as low, TEMP_LOW as not low, and STOP_PB as stop. | N (F-04) | Lift each wire. Verify the response. |
| FR-MXT-015 | On processor fault or output power loss, set FILL_VLV closed, STEAM_VLV closed, and AGITATOR off. | N | Remove output power. Put the processor in program mode. |
| FR-MXT-016 | Overfill, over-temperature, and dry-run protection that goes beyond BPCS logic is defined in the SRS (SRS-MXT, to be created from a hazard review). | N | Review SRS reference. |

## 7. Interlocks and alarms

- **Interlocks:** FR-MXT-005, -010, and -012 are the interlocks. The cause-and-effect chart CE-MXT-001 does not exist yet, so create it from this table. The narrative will then reference it.
- **Alarms:** Reference alarm database ALM-MXT (to be created under ISA-18.2). The alarms needed are fill timeout, steam time limit, and E-stop. The as-found system has only one horn, driven by the fill timeout.

## 8. Abnormal handling

| Condition | Response |
|---|---|
| Bad switch signal | FR-MXT-014 |
| Comms loss | The as-found system has no network. If the upgrade adds an HMI, comms loss shall not change output states. START, STOP, and E-stop stay hardwired. |
| Power loss and restart | All outputs off. Restart in STOPPED. The fill timer clears (FR-MXT-001). |
| Processor fault or output power loss | FR-MXT-015 |

## 9. Operator interface

- **Operator sees:** state (STOPPED, RUNNING, FILL FAULT, E-STOPPED), FILL_VLV, AGITATOR, STEAM_VLV, and alarms.
- **Operator changes:** START, STOP, ACK, and AGIT_HAND (function pending OI-03).
- **Prompts:**
  - "Fill timeout. Check the supply and FILL_VLV. Push STOP. Push START."
  - Warning: "Lock out the tank before you enter. The tank can fill and heat without warning."

## 10. Findings: do not carry forward

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 | R0, B3:0/0 | **High.** The latch is retained through power loss. The tank restarts unattended, which is a personnel hazard. | Use a non-retentive latch or clear it on first scan. Require START after power-up (FR-MXT-001). |
| F-02 | R6 | **High.** START resets the timer at any time. It clears the timeout, silences the horn, and re-opens the fill valve with no acknowledgment. A stuck or jumpered START holds the timer reset and defeats the timeout. | Reset only in STOPPED. Clear faults via STOP then START (FR-MXT-002, -008). |
| F-03 | R2 | **Medium.** The RTO accumulates across all fills in a run, not per fill. Repeated legitimate refills eventually trip it. The accumulated value also survives power loss. | Reset on high level and on STOPPED (FR-MXT-006). Confirm intent (OI-06). |
| F-04 | R1, R4 | **High.** The high-level and temperature inputs are not shown to fail safe. A broken LSH wire could let the fill run on, and a broken TEMP_LOW wire could leave steam on. The 600 s timer is the only overfill backstop, and F-02 defeats it. | Use fail-safe polarity (FR-MXT-014). Assess independent protection in the SRS (FR-MXT-016). |
| F-05 | R3 | **High.** `AGIT_HAND` bypasses the low-level permissive. The agitator can run dry, which risks damage to the seal and shaft. | Remove the bypass (FR-MXT-010, -011). Interview operations first (OI-03). |
| F-06 | R4 | **High.** Steam depends only on the agitator. With F-05 it can open into an empty or low tank. There is no direct level check. | Add LSL_TANK as a direct permissive (FR-MXT-012). |
| F-07 | R4 | **Medium.** There is no steam time limit and no over-temperature protection beyond the single TEMP_LOW input. | Add the time limit (FR-MXT-013). Assess over-temperature in the SRS. |
| F-08 | R5 | **Medium.** The horn is the only alarm. It has no acknowledge and is silenced only by START. There are no alarms for E-stop, steam, or level. | Add ACK and an ISA-18.2 alarm database (FR-MXT-009). |
| F-09 | R0 | **High (verify).** The E-stop is a PLC input only. A PLC input is not a safety function, and outputs may not drop if the PLC or output card fails. | Hardwire E-stop to remove output power. Define it in the SRS (OI-02). |
| F-10 | R3, R4 | **Low.** There is no delay or deadband on LSL_TANK. Agitator and steam can chatter near the low point. | Add on/off delays (SP-MXT-002, -003). |
| F-11 | I:1/3 | **Low.** `LSL_TANK` is ON when the level is above the low point. The name is the opposite of the signal, which invites wiring and programming errors. | Name signals by the healthy condition. Record polarity in the instrument index. |

Carry these forward: the NC STOP button, the E-stop dropping the run latch, the timeout holding the fill valve closed after expiry, and the agitator-before-steam dependency.

## 11. Open items

Owners are roles. Due dates are proposed from today (2026-10-18) and need your confirmation.

| ID | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-01 | Confirm the export is complete: discharge, other B3/N7 bits, first-scan logic. Confirm that refilling on level drop is intended. | Controls lead | 2026-10-30 |
| OI-02 | Verify field polarity of LSH, LSL, TEMP_LOW, and the STOP circuit. Confirm how the E-stop is wired. | Integrator | 2026-10-30 |
| OI-03 | Establish why AGIT_HAND exists and what operators use it for. | Operations lead | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-04 | Decide agitator and steam behavior in FILL FAULT. | Operations lead | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-05 | Run a hazard review for overfill, over-temperature, and dry running. Set SP-MXT-004. | Process safety | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-06 | Confirm the fill timeout value and per-fill versus per-run timing. | Process engineer | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-07 | Assign tag numbers and confirm valve types and fail positions. | Controls lead | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-08 | Get operations sign-off on states and prompts. | Operations lead | Before FDS issue |
